title: Matter brief (triodian.matterBrief/1)
description: The fixed-format brief the AI Obligations Atlas builds in the lawyer's browser and exports for the assessment apps. It lists the obligations in scope by source tier, the questions counsel will need to determine, and the engagements that fit. It contains no statement of what the law requires of the client. Built by the AI Obligations Atlas (obligations-atlas src/core/atlas.js); read by AI Board Direction and AI Use Assessment (public/shared/matter-brief.js). Copied from obligations-atlas schemas/matter-brief.schema.json, which remains the Atlas build check until the Atlas vendors this copy.

briefFormat.description: Format and version, for the loading app

matterLabel.description: The lawyer's own label for the matter; never sent to Triodian

sectors.description: Regulated sectors chosen, from the Metamodel's reference-data/regulated-sectors.json

entityTypes.description: Entity types, from the Metamodel's regulatedEntityType list

useCases.description: Standardised use cases in scope, with the consequence level counsel set for this client

consequenceLevel.description: Consequence C1 to C5 against the client's own thresholds, or null when not set

dataset.description: The Atlas dataset the brief was built from, for audit

obligationsByTier.description: Obligation references grouped by source tier. adopted is present when the brief lists controls of a standard the client has adopted, chosen by the client's Statement of Applicability

binding.description: Law or prudential standard in force

expected.description: Regulator expectation, guidance or recognised standard

anticipated.description: Made but not yet in force, or under consultation

adopted.description: A voluntary standard the client has adopted for itself (for example ISO/IEC 42001:2023 Annex A), listed where the client's Statement of Applicability says it applies

counts.description: Number of references in each tier, and how many are specific to the use cases or apply to any AI use

coverage.description: Jurisdictions in scope the Atlas does not yet cover. No records there does not mean no obligations apply

note.description: What that means for the reader

questionsForCounsel.description: Questions counsel will need to determine

about.description: Use case or obligation the question concerns

engagementsThatFit.description: Engagements that fit the scope: by entity type and sector when either is chosen (see profile), otherwise by the use cases. Counsel decides whether to engage.

useCaseIDs.description: Use cases in scope that lead to it

mode.description: AI Board Direction only: connected for a financially regulated entity (the board's directions bound the AI Risk Appetite engagement), standalone otherwise

reason.description: Why it fits, in plain words

profile.description: regulated when an entity type or sector in scope is financially regulated, general when the scope names others only; absent when it names neither

notices.description: The standing rule and other notices, carried into every export

obligationRef.description: A reference to one Atlas obligation record

appliesToAnyAIUse.description: True when the record applies to any AI use, not only the selected use cases

useCaseIDs.description: Use cases in scope the record reaches

lastVerified.description: Last verified against the official text

publicationStatus.description: published, or pendingReview in preview data

provenanceRef.description: Latest provenance ledger entry for the record

statementOfApplicability.description: For an adopted-standard record: the client's Statement of Applicability row for it, as the brief read it. It stays in the brief and is not sent to the Atlas

applicable.description: Whether the Statement says the control applies

justification.description: The Statement's justification for including or excluding it

implementation.description: How far the Statement says it is implemented
